result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided from one another, from nature, and from our own deepest selves. I would replace it with an unshakable recognition of our interconnectedness, a truth so obvious that it reshapes every system, every interaction, every story we tell.

This isn’t about forced unity or erasing differences, but about seeing that our fates are woven together—our suffering, our joy, our survival. It would mean redesigning economies not around scarcity and competition, but around care and regeneration. It would mean education that teaches empathy as rigorously as math, and justice systems that heal rather than punish. It would mean a politics that serves life, not power.

And perhaps most radically, it would mean a cultural shift where we no longer measure worth by productivity or possession, but by presence, by how deeply we listen, how generously we give, how fiercely we protect what is fragile.

What would *you* change?
